rot.kingInCenter.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: in open positions, with the enemy king still in the center and your pieces developed, every line opened toward it brings one of your pieces in with a gain of time. Open the lines before it castles.
rot.kingInCenter.ideia.ex1.e2: Game Kebabkongen vs Yami04, Lichess. Black is a pawn up, and the pawn on g5 attacks your bishop on h4. The black king is still on e8, and the knight on g8 blocks short castling.
rot.kingInCenter.ideia.ex1.e3: The pawns on f6 and g5 close the f-file and the diagonal from h5 to e8. If one of them leaves, your bishop on e2, your rook on f1 and your queen reach the king.
rot.kingInCenter.ideia.ex1.p: Save the bishop or open lines? Play the move that opens the way to the black king.
rot.kingInCenter.ideia.ex1.certo: Yes: the knight captures the pawn on g5 and gives itself up. If the pawn on f6 takes it, the f-file and the diagonal from h5 to e8 open.
rot.kingInCenter.ideia.ex1.revela: The move is the knight capturing the pawn on g5. It gives itself up to open the f-file and the diagonal from h5 to e8.
rot.kingInCenter.ideia.ex1.err.e5f6.1: The pawn captures on f6, but it leaves the bishop on h4 attacked.
rot.kingInCenter.ideia.ex1.err.e5f6.2: The pawn on g5 captures the bishop: White is a piece down, and no line has opened to the king.
rot.kingInCenter.ideia.ex1.err.volta: Back to the position: look for the move that opens lines to the black king.
rot.kingInCenter.ideia.ex1.err.h4g5.1: The bishop captures the pawn on g5.
rot.kingInCenter.ideia.ex1.err.h4g5.2: The pawn on f6 recaptures. White has given the bishop for a pawn, and the attack is one piece short.
rot.kingInCenter.ideia.ex1.fora: That move opens no line to the black king. If you only save the bishop, Black gains time to close the position with the extra pawn. Look for the move that does.
rot.kingInCenter.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: look for the move that opens lines.
rot.kingInCenter.ideia.ex1.l.1: The knight captures the pawn on g5 and gives itself up.
rot.kingInCenter.ideia.ex1.l.2: The pawn on f6 captures the knight. Now the f-file and the diagonal from h5 to e8 are open.
rot.kingInCenter.ideia.ex1.l.3: The bishop gives check on h5, and no black piece can block. The king has to move and loses the right to castle.
rot.kingInCenter.ideia.ex1.l.4: The king goes to f8, on the file you have just opened.
rot.kingInCenter.ideia.ex1.l.5: The queen gives check along the f-file. One more open line, one more piece arriving with a gain of time.
rot.kingInCenter.ideia.ex1.l.6: The knight on g8 blocks the check on f6.
rot.kingInCenter.ideia.ex1.l.7: The bishop captures the pawn on g5. The knight on f6 is pinned by the queen on f3 and also attacked by the bishop and by the pawn on e5.
rot.kingInCenter.ideia.ex1.l.8: In positions like this, Black's extra pawn is worth little: with the king in the center and no castling, every open line brought a white piece in with check.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.colunaD.1: Attack: let us look together, as White. Game Melis22 vs Chingiz1995, Lichess. Black is two pawns up, but the black king is on e8, unable to castle. Your rook is on the seventh rank, and the queen on d6.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.colunaD.l.1: The pawn on e6 is the king's last shield, and only the bishop on d7 defends it.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.colunaD.l.2: The rook captures the bishop on d7, the defender of e6.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.colunaD.l.4: The queen captures the pawn on e6 with check and attacks both rooks, the one on d7 and the one on g8.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.colunaD.l.5: The king goes to d8 and defends the rook on d7.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.colunaD.l.6: The queen captures the rook on g8 with check. White has won the material back, and the attack goes on.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.colunaD.l.7: In positions like this, the lines to the king were already open: removing one defender was enough for the queen to come in with check.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.antesDoRoque.1: Attack: still White. Game iampulkit vs Kordi50, Lichess, from a Benoni. The black king is on e8 and can castle next move. The black queen is on e7, on the file of your rook on e1.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.antesDoRoque.l.1: The knight on b5 can give check on c7, and from there it attacks e8 and e6. What is missing is to bring the black queen to e6.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.antesDoRoque.l.2: The rook captures the pawn on e6, gives itself up and attacks the queen on e7.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.antesDoRoque.l.3: The queen captures the rook. If Black had castled instead, the rook would have captured the queen.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.antesDoRoque.l.4: The knight gives check on c7 and attacks the queen on e6: it is a fork.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.antesDoRoque.l.5: The king steps out of check.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.antesDoRoque.l.6: The knight captures the queen. White gave up the rook and won the queen.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.antesDoRoque.l.7: One move later, castling would have taken the king off e8, and the fork would not exist. In positions like this, attack the king while it is still in the center.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.centroFechado.1: Attack: back to White. Game otime4planb vs ASzilagyi, Lichess. The black king is on e8, but the center is closed: the pawns on d4 and e5 lock the ones on d5 and e6.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.centroFechado.l.1: The tempting sacrifice is the knight capturing on e6, to open lines to the king.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.centroFechado.l.2: The knight captures the pawn on e6.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.centroFechado.l.3: The bishop recaptures. The pawns on d4, d5 and e5 stay where they are, and no line has opened to the king: White has just lost the knight.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.centroFechado.vol: Back to the position: with the center closed, the sacrifice opens no way, and the king stays sheltered behind the pawns. Look for another target.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.centroFechado.c.1: The knight goes to b7 and attacks the queen on d8.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.centroFechado.c.3: The knight gives check on d6, protected by the pawn on e5.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.centroFechado.c.5: The pawn recaptures, and White wins the queen for a knight.
rot.kingInCenter.demos.centroFechado.c.6: Here the king was in the center, but the closed pawns protected it. The right blow was against the queen, not the king.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.valeAqui.enunci: Now you, with White. Does it work here? Check whether the black king is stuck in the center and whether there are lines to open toward it, and play the best move.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.valeAqui.fim: It works: your bishop on a3 prevented castling, and the queen gave check on h5. Then the bishop gave itself up on g6 to open the h-file, and the queen captured the rook on h8 with check.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.valeAqui.err.f2: The pawn attacks the bishop on e5, but without a check Black gains time. The black king cannot castle: look for the check that takes advantage of that.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.valeAqui.err.b5: The knight gives check on c7, but the queen on d8 takes it, and no line opens to the king. Look for the check that opens the way.
The knight gives check on d6, but the bishop on e5 takes it, and no line opens to the king. Look for the check that opens the way.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.valeAqui.err.d3: The bishop gives check on g6, but the pawn on h7 takes it, and your queen cannot reach the h-file yet. First bring the queen in with check.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.valeAqui.err.f1: The rook takes the d-file, but without a check Black gains time. Look for the queen check.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.valeAqui.err.re: The queen retreats, and the black king gains time. The pawn on h7 closes the h-file and defends g6: give up a piece on g6 to pull it away.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.valeAqui.err.h5: The queen captures on g6 with check, but it wins nothing. The h-file is open: capture the rook on h8 with check.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.naoVale.enuncia: White again, and the same question: does it work here? The black king is on e8, and the pawn on h6 attacks your knight on g5. Look at the center before giving up a piece near the king, and play the best move.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.naoVale.fim: It did not work: with the center locked, giving up a piece near the king opened no way. The target was the queen on e7: attacked by the bishop on a3, it could not escape without losing material.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.naoVale.err.g5f: The knight gives itself up on f7, and the queen on e7 takes it. The central pawns stay locked, and no line has opened to the king. Look for another target.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.naoVale.err.g5e: The knight gives itself up on e6, and the queen on e7 takes it. The central pawns stay locked, and no line has opened to the king. Look for another target.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.naoVale.err.d3g: The bishop gives itself up on g6, and the pawn on f7 takes it. With the center locked, no line has opened to the king. Look for another target.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.naoVale.err.f3f: The queen gives check on f7, but the black queen takes it.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.naoVale.err.g5e: The knight gives itself up on e4, and the pawn on d5 takes it. Look for another target.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.naoVale.err.g5h: The knight escapes, but that wins nothing. Look at the queen on e7: where can it escape to?
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.naoVale.err.dam: The bishop on a3 still attacks the queen on e7: take it.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.colunaH.enuncia: Now let us think from Black's side. The white king is still on e1, and the bishop on g5 attacks your queen. Your rook on h8 is on the h-file, closed by the pawn on h4. Play the best move.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.colunaH.fim: The queen captured the bishop on g5 and gave itself up to open the h-file. The rook gave check on h1 and, after the king moved, captured the queen on d1: Black came out ahead in material.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.colunaH.err.f8e: The bishop blocks the attack on the queen, but the bishop on g5 captures it, and the h-file stays closed. Look for the move that opens the file.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.colunaH.err.f7f: The pawn attacks the bishop, but White trades on f6, and the h-file stays closed. Look for the move that opens the file.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.colunaH.err.d8b: The queen gets out of the attack, but the h-file stays closed by the pawn on h4. Look for the move that opens it.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.colunaH.err.dam: The queen gets out of the attack, but the h-file stays closed by the pawn on h4. Look for the move that opens it.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.colunaH.err.xeq: The h-file is open and the white king is on e1: give the rook check.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.colunaH.err.cap: The rook on h1 is on the same rank as the queen on d1: capture it.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.xequeDuplo.enun: Back to White. Black is threatening your king, but the black king is still on e8, and the f-file is open. Play the best move.
rot.kingInCenter.pratica.xequeDuplo.fim: The queen gave check on f7, and the bishop left d2 with a double check: its own from g5 and the one from the rook on d1. Then the rook gave mate on d8.
The king captures the pawn on c2, but Black gains time to attack. Use the checks against the black king first.
The queen gives check on f8, but the king captures it.
That gives the black king time. The bishop on d2 stands in front of the rook on d1: move it away with check.
The bishop moves and uncovers the rook check, but it is a single check: the pawn on c2 takes the rook on d1, and Black escapes. Take the bishop to a square where it also gives check.
